blocks.task_summary: Find the mode of the continuous random variable X with the given probability density function f.
method_path: Recognize mode is the value of x at which f(x) attains its maximum
Find maximum via f'(x)=0, axis of symmetry, or graph of f

evidence.basis: recognizes that the mode is a value of x at which f has a maximum value (M1); a clearly labelled graph of f OR states f'(x)=0 OR considers the axis of symmetry; mode is 1.5 (kg) A1

blocks.task_summary: Find P(1 ≤ X ≤ 2) by integrating the probability density function f over [1, 2].
method_path: Set up the definite integral of f(x) from 1 to 2
Evaluate the integral (analytically or via GDC)

evidence.basis: attempts to find integral from 1 to 2 of f(x) dx (M1); 0.435294... = 37/85 = 0.435 A1

blocks.task_summary: Find the median m of X by solving the equation P(X ≤ m) = 0.5, i.e. integral from 0.5 to m of f(x) dx = 0.5.
method_path: Recognize median m satisfies integral from 0.5 to m of f(x) dx = 0.5
Solve the resulting equation for m
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: explicit antiderivative with algebraic simplification leading to the same equation

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: recognizes that integral from 0.5 to m of f(x) dx = 0.5 (M1); m = 1.68701..., m = 1.69 (kg) A2. METHOD 2: same recognition (M1); explicit integration with algebraic work (A1); m = 1.69 (kg) A1.

blocks.task_summary: Find the probability that a randomly selected customer spends at most $48, given $25/kg normally and $24/kg discounted rate for weight at least 0.75 kg.
method_path: Translate spend ≤ $48: for weight < 0.75 kg (rate $25/kg) always satisfied; for weight ≥ 0.75 kg (rate $24/kg) need weight ≤ 2 kg
Set up and evaluate integral of f(x) from 0.5 to 2

evidence.basis: 0.5 ≤ x ≤ 2 (can be seen in a definite integral) (A1); attempts to evaluate their definite integral (M1); integral from 0.5 to 2 of f(x) dx = 0.635294... = 0.635 A1

blocks.task_summary: Find the expected amount spent per customer to the nearest cent, using piecewise rates $25/kg for weight < 0.75 kg and $24/kg for weight ≥ 0.75 kg.
method_path: Form expected value as sum of piecewise integrals: 25 times integral of x f(x) from 0.5 to 0.75 plus 24 times integral of x f(x) from 0.75 to 3
Compute integral of x f(x) from 0.5 to 0.75
Compute integral of x f(x) from 0.75 to 3
Multiply by respective rates and sum

evidence.basis: an attempt at forming an expected value integral (M1); integral from 0.5 to 0.75 of x f(x) dx = 0.060592... OR 25 times that = 1.51482... (A1); integral from 0.75 to 3 of x f(x) dx = 1.64345... OR 24 times that = 39.4428... (A1); sums their two definite integrals (M1); expected amount = $40.96 A1
